correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary center z=t*1+w with w orthogonal to 1, averaging squared distances over the complete weight-s layer gives q_s(t)+||w||^2, where q_s(t)=d*t^2+s(1-2t). A diagonal center attains q_s(t) exactly on that layer, so the full MEB problem reduces without relaxation to minimizing max_s q_s(t). Because q_s is affine in s, only a=min S and b=max S can control the maximum. The resulting two-piece convex objective has the unique minimizer stated in the claim. Exact differences between the controlling extreme layer and every other layer give the contact classification, while the positive ||w||^2 term proves uniqueness off the diagonal.

value.rationale: S-hypersimplices are a named geometry family encompassing cubes, simplices, ordinary hypersimplices, crosspolytopes, and halfcubes. The theorem gives a complete natural Euclidean invariant for every member: center, radius, uniqueness, and contact set. The endpoint-only dependence is structurally informative because arbitrary insertion or deletion of intermediate Hamming layers leaves the MEB unchanged, and the exact midpoint transition distinguishes an extreme-layer-controlled regime from an all-vertex cospherical regime.
